summary: This Wikipedia article describes Schlumberger (doing business as SLB), an American oilfield services company founded in 1926 in Paris by brothers Conrad and Marcel Schlumberger and headquartered in Houston, Texas. It covers the company's history of acquisitions and divestitures, its corporate presence in France and the United States, a 2009 Newsweek green ranking, and several controversies including radioactive source losses, spills, PCB contamination, its role in the Deepwater Horizon well, sanctions violations with Iran and Sudan, a 2020 sexual harassment lawsuit, and its operations in Russia.
one_line: Schlumberger (now SLB) is an American oilfield services company founded in Paris in 1926, known for its history, expansion, and controversies.
key_facts: Schlumberger was founded in 1926 in Paris as the Electric Prospecting Company by brothers Conrad and Marcel Schlumberger from Alsace.
The first-ever electrical resistivity well log was recorded by Schlumberger in Merkwiller-Pechelbronn, France, in 1927.
Schlumberger became listed on the New York Stock Exchange on February 2, 1962.
Schlumberger Limited was incorporated as a holding company in 1956.
In 1999, Schlumberger and Smith International created the joint venture M-I L.L.C., the world's largest drilling fluids company, with a 40% Schlumberger stake.
In 2006, Schlumberger purchased the remaining 30% of WesternGeco from Baker Hughes for US$2.4 billion.
In 2010, the acquisition of Smith International was announced in an all-stock deal valued at $11.3 billion and completed on August 27, 2010.
In 2015, Schlumberger pled guilty to violating U.S. sanctions related to Iran and Sudan and agreed to pay a $237 million penalty.
In 2015, Schlumberger announced 21,000 layoffs, accounting for 15% of the company's total workforce.
In 2022, Schlumberger completed a corporate rebranding to be known as SLB.
In April 2024, SLB announced its intention to acquire ChampionX in an all-stock deal valued at $7.75 billion.
In 2020, a class action lawsuit alleged a culture of sexual harassment, discrimination, and retaliation at Schlumberger.
Schlumberger's headquarters moved from New York to Houston in 2005, and it planned in 2015 to move its U.S. headquarters to Sugar Land, Texas.
In 2010, the Aberdeen Sheriff court fined Schlumberger Oilfield UK £300,000 for losing a radioactive source on the rig floor on the Ensco 101 mobile drilling rig in the North Sea.
In March 2022, Schlumberger stopped investing in its projects in Russia because of international sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War.
